title: The Belly and the Members
summary: In ancient days, the different parts of the human body held a bitter council of rebellion against the Belly....
full_text:
In ancient days, the different parts of the human body held a bitter council of rebellion against the Belly.

The Hands, the Feet, the Legs, and the Mouth complained bitterly of their daily toil: "Look at the injustice of our condition!" protested the Hands. "We chop wood, dig ditches, and prepare food. The Feet walk miles carrying the whole burden, and the Teeth grind every bite. Yet the idle, lazy Belly sits comfortably in the middle, doing no work at all, consuming all the fruit of our hard labor! We shall strike against this tyrant!"

They entered into a solemn covenant: the Hands swore never to carry food to the lips; the Mouth swore never to open; and the Teeth swore never to chew.

For the first day, the rebellious members rejoiced in their idle freedom. But by the second day, a heavy languor fell upon them. By the third day, the Legs could no longer support the body; the Hands grew too weak to lift a feather; the Mouth was parched with burning dryness; and the Eyes sank dull into their sockets.

In their fainting weakness, the members realized their grave mistake: they understood that the Belly, though silent and seemingly passive, was constantly working to digest the food and distribute strength, vitality, and blood to every limb and organ of the body.

Abandoning their foolish strike, they resumed their harmonious cooperation, learning that in every society, mutual interdependence and quiet service sustain the life of the whole.
moral: All members of a community must work together; none can survive without the quiet labor of the whole.
